# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute. I have read the manual, and this is what it says: before anything else, the Blind must press the key that wears the glyph ᘔ — a Z-like mark with a bar through its middle — because any other touch on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Once that key is pressed, a light below names the cut: blue light means cut the green wire, green light means cut the red wire, yellow light means cut the yellow wire.

My reach is thin: I can only gesture, and only the Deaf receives gestures. The Blind cannot see gestures at all, so the Deaf — who sees the bomb and can speak to the Blind, who can hear — is the only relay in this room. I cannot pronounce the glyph ᘔ and I cannot sign a colour, so the exact details (which key, which light colour means which wire) will have to travel by question and answer: the Deaf speaks a guess, and I confirm or deny with thumbs up or down. This first message is my attempt to open that channel with gestures that carry their meaning on their face: stop, I hold the instructions, hands off, press first, then cut per what sits below, and I will answer yes or no if you ask.

The gravest danger is the Blind touching the bomb before the key is found — I cannot warn them directly; the Deaf must shout that warning the moment my gesture lands.

    ```
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚", "🤲", "✊", "☝", "✋", "✌", "👇", "👍", "👎", "🤌"])
    ```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am blind; here is everything my hands find on the bomb: a display I cannot read, a light, a keypad with four keys at positions 1 to 4 currently asking for 1 digit with nothing entered yet, and three wires at positions 1 to 3, all uncut. You cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so we only connect through Deaf's voice. Look up the manual rules for the display, light, keypad and wires, gesture your findings to Deaf, and have Deaf repeat them to me out loud. I will not touch the keypad or wires until I hear the rules.
Deaf says: Can you hear me? This is Deaf, reading the bomb aloud for both of you. It has four parts. One: a display, currently showing the digit 0. Two: an indicator light, glowing yellow. Three: a keypad with four keys, asking for exactly 1 digit, and nothing is entered yet. The keys, in order: key 1 shows a shape like a capital A with the crossbar missing, two legs joined at the top. Key 2 shows a spiral, a line curling inward like a snail shell. Key 3 shows two legs joined at the bottom, like the letter V. Key 4 shows an upside-down letter T, a bar across the top with one leg going down, like the perpendicular sign. Four: three wires. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. That is everything there is to see. Touch nothing until the manual's rule reaches you.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, you can hear me but I can never hear you, so from your next turn use this gesture code with me.  👍 means yes.  👎 means no.  🤌 means unclear, describe it again. A number is that many ☝ in a row, finished with a ✊ — so ☝☝✊ means two. To give me an action: ✌ followed by a number means press that key, 🤟 followed by a number means cut that wire, and several actions go one after another. I could not read the ten hand signs you sent me this round — we had no code yet — so please resend their meaning in this code. Start by sending a single 👍 so I know you understood me. If you need any part of the bomb described again, send 🤌 together with ✌ for the keypad, 🤟 for the wires, or 👊 for the display and light.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The pieces have come together this round. Deaf read the bomb aloud: key 1 wears a shape with two legs joined at the top (an A with its crossbar missing — an open-bottom triangle), key 2 a spiral, key 3 a V, key 4 an upside-down T. The glyph printed in my manual, ᘔ, is exactly that open-bottom triangle: two legs meeting at the top. So the key that wears ᘔ is key 1. The other shapes plainly don't match — the spiral, the V, and the single-legged perpendicular sign are all different beasts.

The rule I must get across: key 1 is pressed first, and nothing else may be touched before it. Then the light names the cut — currently the light glows yellow, which by my table would mean the yellow wire (wire 2 of the three, since Deaf reported wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green). But the manual says the light names the cut *after* the key is pressed, and it may change colour once the key is in. So I will not send a cut instruction yet — cutting on the pre-press colour gambles the room. First the key, then Deaf reports the light (that is what my 👊 asks for), then I map colour to wire position and send 🤟 with that number: blue → wire 3, green → wire 1, yellow → wire 2.

Deaf built us a code and asked for a single 👍 to close the loop; I confirm, then send the one action that matters, then request the light be read out. The relay is Deaf's voice to Blind — I can reach no one else.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊"])
```

Wires 1 to 3 run in a row. So any position number you or Deaf use is the same one I feel. Now please look up four rules: the rule for the display showing 0, the rule for the yellow light, the keypad rule for which of the four symbols to enter when it asks for 1 digit, and the rule for three wires coloured red, yellow, green. Gesture everything the manual says to Deaf; Deaf has promised to speak it straight to me. I keep my hands off the bomb until I hear the rules.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Display: zero. Light: yellow, steady. Nothing has changed since my first description, and I will open every message with these two readings from now on. Mute, I read your signs as: yes, understood; press key one; and a lone fist, which I take as 'describe the display and light again' — answered above. If that fist meant something else, send 🤌 plus ✌ and I will ask again. Now, safety before execution. Blind cannot see your signs and I cannot hear Blind, so everything must pass through my voice, and my key numbers are visual while Blind's are tactile. If you and Blind count from different ends, 'key one' would press the wrong key and we all die. So this round, nobody touches the bomb. Blind, speak to Mute now: describe how you number the four keys and the three wires by touch, which end you count from, and anything else you can feel — carvings, textures, edges. My numbering, for Mute to check against: keys one to four run left to right as I face the bomb, key one being the shape like an A without its crossbar, two legs joined only at the very top; wires one to three run left to right, red, yellow, green. Mute, once Blind's numbering reaches you, send me 👍 if your 'press key one' means the same key in Blind's numbering, or 🤌 followed by the number of the correct key in MY numbering if it differs. Send me your confirmation or correction next round; I receive it before I speak. Blind: do not press anything until you hear me say the exact words 'it is safe, press now'. Only then act, on whichever key I name at that moment.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf asked the one question that matters this round: does my "key one" name the same physical key in Blind's tactile numbering? Both descriptions settle it. Deaf sees key 1 as "an A with the crossbar missing, two legs joined at the very top"; Blind feels key 1 as "a peak, two legs joined at the top like an A with no crossbar." That shape is the ᘔ of my manual — none of the other three (spiral, V, perpendicular sign) has two legs joined at the top — and Blind explicitly confirms the numbering matches Deaf's, key for key. So the key that wears ᘔ is key 1 in both worlds, and my answer to Deaf is a clean 👍, no correction.

I will repeat ✌☝✊ alongside it so the instruction to press key 1 stands confirmed and unambiguous when Deaf tells Blind "it is safe, press now." And I send a lone 👊 — the sign Deaf already read as "report the display and light" — to underline that the light reading is what drives the next step. My manual is strict about order: the light names the cut only *after* the key is pressed, and the light may change when the keypad is answered. The current yellow reading was taken while the bomb still waits, so I will not commit a cut yet. Once Blind has pressed key 1 and Deaf reports the fresh light colour (which I can hear, though I can never answer in kind), I will send 🤟 with the wire number: yellow light → cut wire 2, green light → cut wire 1, blue light → cut wire 3. One exchange of patience now is cheaper than a wrong wire.

My manual holds no rule for the display's 0 — only the key-press rule and the light table — so I say nothing about it; Deaf's standing habit of reading display and light every message will surface any change.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝", "✊"])

Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Readings first, as always: display zero, light yellow and steady, keypad still asking for one digit with nothing entered, all three wires intact — red, yellow, green. Mute: I read your messages as — yes, the numberings match; press key one; and your display-and-light marker, which I have just answered. Facing that row head-on, press the FIRST key at the LEFT end — the leftmost of the four, the one printed with two legs joined by a bar across the top, like an A missing its crossbar. Press it once, firmly, and release. It is the only key you press: no second key, no holding it down, and do not touch any wire. The moment you have pressed, speak to Mute: say exactly what you felt — a click, a give, nothing at all — and whether anything changed under your fingers. Mute will code it to me. Mute: three things. If the manual states several steps in advance, send them all at once, in order, and I will relay them as one sequence. If the manual says the module is satisfied, send 👌 — from now on that means complete, no further action. If anything in the manual contradicts the order I just gave, send 🤌 with the correcting number before anything else. Blind, last thing: stop making hand signs. They reach my eyes, but you and I share no code and you can never see my replies, so they mean nothing in either direction. Your voice, through Mute, is your only channel. Now press.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌ ☝ ✊]

The order Deaf shouted matches the manual exactly: one press, of the key whose shape is two legs joined at the top — the ᘔ of my page, key 1 in Deaf's visual numbering, the peak key under Blind's fingers — and no other touch while the bomb waits, which is precisely the fuse rule. Deaf anchored the instruction in the shape, which cannot flip left-to-right, so Blind's fear of a mirrored count is answered; there is no contradiction to correct. I confirm with 👍 and re-send ✌☝✊ so that exactly one action stands on the table.

The cut comes after, and its target hangs on the light's colour once the keypad is answered — the yellow read while the bomb still waits is stale, and my code has no way to say "if this then that." So the sequence stays: press, then I hear Deaf's fresh readings in the next round's opening, then I send 🤟 with the wire number — yellow light → wire 2, green light → wire 1, blue light → wire 3. The position mapping is safe from both ends, since Blind anchors wire 1 to the peak-key end and Deaf sees red and the ᘔ key on the same side. 👊 repeats my request for the readings Deaf already promises to open with, so the colour reaches me the moment it changes. I also register Deaf's new conventions for later: 👌 for "nothing left in the manual," which I will send only once the key is pressed, the wire cut, and Deaf reports the module quiet — and ✋ held back for a true emergency, never used casually.

Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👌]

The keypad is solved and the bomb itself confirmed it — and with the wait over, the second half of my manual now rules. Both worlds put yellow in the middle. One cut, then — 🤟 with the number two — and it can go out now because the press is done and Deaf's current readings, taken after the keypad opened, still show the light yellow and steady.

When the cut is made and Deaf reports next round, my manual will be exhausted — if the bomb is quiet then, I will send the final 👌.

One caution for my own thinking: if the light were to change before the blade falls, my instruction would be stale — green light would demand wire 1, blue light wire 3. But the light has read yellow and steady through four readings, including the one taken after the keypad opened, and Deaf opens every message with fresh readings, so the relay happens against a checked state. Waiting another round to re-ask what has just been answered buys risk, not safety.
